title: Effective Cartier presentation of a line bundle on a Noetherian quasi-affine scheme
statement: Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open covering has a finite subcover). Suppose $V$ admits an open immersion into an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. For every invertible $\mathcal O_V$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there is an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset V$ with $M\cong\mathcal O_V(D)$, where an effective Cartier divisor and its associated invertible module are as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The empty scheme and the empty divisor are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0AYM (lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier), quasi-affine clause: the second divisor can be empty.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-associated-points-finite] to $V$, using the locally Noetherian and quasi-compact hypotheses. Thus $E=\operatorname{Ass}(V)$ is a finite subset of $V$, including all embedded associated points, not just the generic points of its irreducible components.

source.place: Tag 05AF, lemma-finite-ass, specialized to the coherent structure sheaf and the quasi-compact open X itself.

proof.text: The given open immersion into an affine scheme, together with quasi-compactness, meets precisely the quasi-affine hypotheses of [lem-sfb-quasiaffine-invertible-finite-set-section]. Apply it to $X=V$, $L=M$ and the finite set $E$ of Step 1. Obtain $s\in\Gamma(V,M)$ whose image in $M_x/\mathfrak m_xM_x$ is nonzero for every associated point $x$ of $V$. Neither affineness of $V$ nor closedness of these points is required.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, with W=X and retaining the nonvanishing conclusion. Quasi-affine means quasi-compact and isomorphic to an open of an affine scheme, as in definition-quasi-affine.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-invertible-section-associated-criterion] to $(V,M,s)$, using local Noetherianity of $V$ and the nonvanishing from Step 2. On every affine trivializing open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, write $s|_U=ae$. Multiplication by $a$ on $A$ is injective, so each such coefficient is a nonzerodivisor. This is exactly the regularity needed to construct a Cartier ideal.

source.place: Tag 0AYL, lemma-regular-section-associated-points; the affine coefficient formulation of regularity is lemma-regular-section-structure-sheaf, Tag 01WZ.

proof.text: Set $D=Z(s)$ by [def-pc-zero-scheme]. On an affine trivialization $M|_U=\mathcal O_Ue$ with dual basis $e^\vee$, the defining evaluation map sends $e^\vee$ to $a$, so its image ideal is $(a)$. By Step 3 these local generators are nonzerodivisors. Hence this ideal is an effective Cartier ideal by [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and $D$ is an effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The final assertion of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] now gives $M\cong\mathcal O_V(Z(s))=\mathcal O_V(D)$. If $V$ is empty the same construction has empty zero scheme and the assertions hold on the empty affine covering. A nowhere-vanishing $s$ gives the unit ideal and empty divisor, which is permitted.

source.place: Tag 0AYM, lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier, quasi-affine paragraph; zero-scheme evaluation and Tag 01X0, lemma-characterize-OD (2).
